system-user.title: Users
system-user.description: User list, creation, status changes and deletion against the new iam/users endpoints. The level model is gone; ownership is expressed through departments.
system-user.scopeSuperAdminTitle: Signed in as a platform-level account
system-user.scopeSuperAdmin: The session carries no tenant, so no tenant filter is offered. List scope and creatable departments are still decided upstream; this page only avoids entry points that hit known gaps.
system-user.scopeTenantAdminTitle: Signed in as a tenant-level account
system-user.scopeTenantAdmin: The session carries a tenant, so the upstream limits the list to what you may see; cross-tenant operations are rejected upstream.
system-user.scopeUnknownTitle: Signed in as an unknown identity
system-user.scopeUnknown: The session has no user info yet (signed out or still loading). The list scope is whatever the upstream returns; this page infers nothing.
system-user.keywordPlaceholder: Search username, display name or email
system-user.detailEmpty: Select a user on the left to see the details
system-user.detailEmptyHint: The list and the details are the two panes of this page; on narrow screens picking a user opens the details and Back returns to the list.
system-user.immutableHint: The username is fixed once created; display name, email and department can be updated through PUT /iam/users/{id}, and the department carries the tenant.
system-user.selectionMissingTitle: That user is not in the current results
system-user.selectionMissing: “{id}” from the link is not in the current filter / page of results. To keep the filters and the address bar consistent, this page will not page around to find it.
system-user.loadFailed: Could not load the user list
system-user.changeStatusHint: Enable or disable this user (disabled users cannot sign in)
system-user.deleteHint: Soft-delete this user (deleted_at); it disappears from the list
system-user.selfHint: You cannot do this to yourself: disabling or deleting your own account locks you out immediately

createForm.title: New user
createForm.description: The new generation only needs a username and a password; tenant ownership comes from the selected department (the request body has no tenant_id).
createForm.usernameHint: 2–64 characters: letters, digits, underscore, dot, hyphen
createForm.displayNameHint: Optional; the list falls back to the username
createForm.emailHint: Optional; used for notifications and password resets
createForm.departmentHint: Departments carry the tenant: picking one fixes the user's tenant
createForm.passwordHint: 6–128 characters (measured upstream); the user should change it after the first sign-in

statusModal.disableDescription: Once {name} is disabled, that user cannot sign in.
statusModal.enableDescription: Once {name} is enabled, that user can sign in again.
statusModal.deleteDescription: Deleting {name} removes the user from the list.
statusModal.disableHint: A disabled user cannot sign in but the record stays; use delete to remove it entirely.
statusModal.deleteHint: This is a soft delete (deleted_at): the account leaves the list and can no longer sign in. It cannot be undone from this page.

system-log.title: Logs
system-log.description: Audit log: list, detail, hash-chain verification and export jobs. The upstream decides the data scope by identity (a super admin sees the whole platform, a tenant admin only its own tenant, filtered upstream), and the page states that scope explicitly.
system-log.emptyFiltered: No entries match the current filters
system-log.loadFailed: Failed to load the audit log
system-log.detailFailed: Failed to load the log detail
system-log.selectHint: Pick an entry on the left to see its detail

filter.title: Filters
filter.reversed: The start is later than the end: the upstream returns an empty set for a reversed range. Fix the range before filtering.

scope.title: Visible scope
scope.superAdmin: A super admin sees the whole platform audit log, can verify the hash chain and create export jobs. Authorisation still happens upstream (NMCPS-REC-004).
scope.tenantAdmin: A tenant admin sees the log after the upstream tenant filter (only actions of accounts inside its own tenant). Data outside that scope never appears in the list, and there is no cross-tenant switch.

detail.snapshotsHint: These three fields measured as empty strings on every entry: the page still renders them when they carry a value, but never read an empty one as "nothing changed" (NMCPS-REC-004 UP-AUD-09).

verify.hint: Verifies the hash chain inside the current time window (the full chain when no window is set). Note that verification writes an audit entry itself.
verify.empty: No entries in {window}, so 0 were checked: an empty window is "intact" only because nothing was verified (NMCPS-REC-004 UP-AUD-05)
verify.broken: Chain broken at entry #{index} of the whole chain ({count} entries checked in {window}). That index is the chain position, not a list row.
verify.needRange: Verification needs both a start and an end time, or neither

export.title: Export audit log
export.description: Creates an asynchronous export job for a time window.
export.hint: The upstream produces the file asynchronously and exposes no progress endpoint: after creating a job, use "Refresh jobs" to see whether downloadUrl is ready (NMCPS-REC-004 UP-AUD-07).
export.name: Job name
export.reversed: The start is later than the end, so the upstream would export an empty result
export.scopeHint: Inherited filters: category {category}, account {account} (adjust the window before submitting)
export.failed: Could not create the export job

errors.reversed: The start cannot be later than the end

errors.forbidden: Session expired or no permission (the upstream reports both as 10201, NMCPS-REC-004 UP-AUD-01): sign in again and retry
errors.notFound: That entry does not exist, or has been purged
errors.invalidParam: Invalid parameters: check the time format and paging values
errors.internal: Upstream internal error: most often a missing required export field (NMCPS-REC-004 UP-AUD-06)

system-permission.description: Roles and their permission matrix. The upstream only exposes list roles / list permissions / grant / revoke / create role / delete role — no role update, no status change and no readable account-role binding, so this page offers none of those.
system-permission.title: Permissions
system-permission.scopeSuperAdmin: The policy domain is closed to super admins: every role and permission endpoint returns 401 (10201). This page sends no requests and offers no actions (NMCPS-REC-003 UP-POL-08).
system-permission.scopeTenantAdmin: You see the tenant's own roles plus the platform built-in templates. Built-in roles are shared read-only templates: grant, revoke and delete are all rejected upstream, so they are displayed without switches.
system-permission.scopeUnknown: The session accountLevel is neither 0 nor 1 (the upstream accepts 2–4 but assigns them no meaning). The page falls back to least privilege: read-only, no write entry points.
system-permission.empty: No roles match the current filter
system-permission.detailEmpty: Select a role on the left to inspect its permissions
system-permission.detailEmptyHint: The list and the detail share this page; on narrow screens selecting a role opens the detail and Back returns to the list.
system-permission.selectionMissingTitle: That role is not in the current results
system-permission.selectionMissing: “{id}” from the link is not part of the current filter / page. To keep the filter and the address bar consistent, the page will not page through results to find it.
system-permission.loadFailed: Failed to load the role list
system-permission.builtinHint: Built-in roles are shared across tenants: grant returns 40307, revoke 40305 and delete 40303, all rejected upstream — so the UI shows them without edit controls.
system-permission.customHint: Custom role permissions apply immediately per switch: there is no Save button, and a revoke cannot be undone — the permission has to be granted again.

matrix.title: Permission matrix
matrix.hint: Resource permissions (device, metric, MIB, alert…) on the left, API permissions on the right; each column is grouped by resource type and every switch is saved immediately (no “save” button). The upstream read-back has no effect field, so a granted permission here means “granted”, not allow-vs-deny.
matrix.loadFailed: Failed to load the permission matrix

createForm.title: New role
createForm.description: A role level must stay below your own: a tenant admin can create L2–L4; L0 / L1 or L5+ are rejected upstream.
createForm.roleCodeHint: 3–64 chars, letters, digits, underscore and hyphen only; cannot be changed after creation
createForm.roleLevelHint: A lower number means more privilege; must stay below your own level
createForm.descriptionPlaceholder: Optional: what this role is for

deleteModal.title: Delete role
deleteModal.description: Deleting {name} also drops every permission granted to it.
deleteModal.hint: The upstream has no restore endpoint: deletion is final — the role has to be recreated and re-granted.

system-policy.description: ABAC rule inspection and access dry run. The upstream has no create/update/delete endpoint for rules, so this page is read-only and offers no write entry points.
system-policy.title: Policies
system-policy.scopeSuperAdmin: The policy domain is closed to super admins: the rule and dry-run endpoints all return 401 (10201). This page sends no requests and offers no actions (NMCPS-REC-003 UP-POL-08).
system-policy.scopeTenantAdmin: You see this tenant's ABAC rules and can use the access dry run to check whether an account can reach an endpoint. The rules themselves are read-only: the upstream has no update or delete endpoint.
system-policy.scopeUnknown: The session accountLevel is neither 0 nor 1 (the upstream accepts 2–4 but assigns them no meaning). The page falls back to least privilege: read-only, no write entry points.
system-policy.detailEmpty: Select a rule on the left to inspect its condition
system-policy.detailEmptyHint: The list and the detail share this page; on narrow screens selecting a rule opens the detail and Back returns to the list.
system-policy.selectionMissingTitle: That rule is not in the current results
system-policy.selectionMissing: “{id}” from the link no longer matches the current search. To keep the search and the address bar consistent, the page will not clear the search to find it.
system-policy.loadFailed: Failed to load the rule list
system-policy.copyFailed: Copy failed: the browser denied clipboard access
system-policy.dslHint: Conditions are govaluate expressions and the upstream does not validate their syntax: a broken expression still saves, so this page shows it verbatim instead of “fixing” it.
system-policy.readonly: The upstream has no create / update / delete endpoint for rules (404 when probed): a rule that is created can neither be edited nor reclaimed, so this page offers no creation entry and enabling is only possible by changing the database upstream.

dryrun.title: Access dry run
dryrun.description: Evaluate the real rules once: can this account reach this endpoint? Nothing is persisted.
dryrun.hint: The verdict combines RBAC and ABAC. The upstream accepts clientIp / deviceCode / resourceTags / accountLevel but they do not affect the result, so this form does not offer them.
dryrun.accountsTruncated: Only the first {listed} of {total} accounts are listed
dryrun.accountsFailed: Failed to load the account list
dryrun.pathHint: Must be the full upstream path, including the /api/v1 prefix
dryrun.noFields: The upstream returned no field whitelist (always null)

errors.pathPrefix: The path must start with /api/v1/ — otherwise it is reported as unauthorized

errors.duplicateCode: That code already exists, pick another one
errors.escalation: A role level must stay below your own level
errors.builtinLocked: Built-in objects are shared read-only templates
errors.invalidParam: Invalid parameter, please check the values
errors.internal: Upstream internal error: usually a missing required field

user-security.title: Security
user-security.description: Manage your sign-in password. Every request is proxied by the BFF to the auth service, and credentials never reach browser storage.
user-security.loginRequiredHint: Security settings need an active session; you will be returned here after signing in.
user-security.mfaUnavailable: The upstream iam service exposes no multi-factor endpoints (NMCPS-ADR-0018 gap G8), so binding and confirmation are offline; this page now covers self-service password change only.
user-security.mfaHint: Register the secret below in any authenticator app; sign-in then also requires a 6-digit code.
user-security.mfaBindWarn: Rebinding invalidates the current one-time codes immediately, so already paired authenticators can no longer sign in. Continue?
user-security.mfaCopyFailed: Copy failed, select the text manually
user-security.mfaUriHint: The link lives in page memory only and dies on reload; the secret is shown exactly once.
user-security.mfaCodeInvalid: Wrong one-time code, check the authenticator clock and retry
user-security.passwordHint: The current session stays valid; if the upstream revokes tokens afterwards, the next request refreshes automatically.
user-security.newPasswordPlaceholder: At least 8 characters, mix case and symbols
user-security.newPasswordSame: The new password must differ from the current one
user-security.confirmPasswordMismatch: The two passwords do not match
